plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Years 5 and 6, Number and Algebra: whole-year revision of the number and algebra questions on tomorrow's Grade 5 and Grade 6 General Maths tests
plan.shape: consolidation: one slide per test question type, attempted first on boards, then the method modelled on the reveal, because all of it has been taught this year
plan.criticalFeature: read what the question really asks (how many are needed, how much is left) before you calculate, then check the answer makes sense
decisionPoints: the launch: which topic each student feels least sure about
the boats remainder check and the times-before-plus hinge
plan.anchor: Read it. Work it. Check it.
plan.catchUp: Missed it? Each slide is one test question type, so start them on the Supported Worksheet and go through the matching slide with them

studentTools: Printed Revision Worksheet for everyone; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: Write the anchor on the board: Read it. Work it. Check it.

resources.label: Revision Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. The trickiest number and algebra question types again, with new numbers.
resources.title: Number and Algebra Revision
resources.subtitle: Read it. Work it. Check it.

items.prompt: Order from smallest to largest: 3.6, 0.36, 3.06, 0.6, 3.606
Find A, B and C.

example.prompt: A van holds 9 people. 50 people need a ride. How many vans?
steps: The 5 left over still need a ride.

items.prompt: Emma's bills are $627 and $289. Is the total a little more or a little less than $900?
items.explain: 600 + 300 = 900. 627 was rounded down by more than 289 was rounded up, so the total (916) is a little more.

items.prompt: A dog walker walks 6 dogs a day for 5 days. She charges $15 for each dog walk. How much does she earn?
Leo had $95.50. He bought a book for $18.25 and a hat for $24.40. How much is left?
Zoe worked out how many cars are needed for 38 people, with 4 in each car. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: 10 cars. The 2 people left over need a car too.

sections.title: Missing numbers, rules and number types

items.prompt: Find each missing number.
Which rule makes 4, 9, 14, 19 for terms 1 to 4?
items.explain: Term 1: 1 x 5 - 1 = 4. Term 4: 4 x 5 - 1 = 19. The other rules only fit some terms.

items.prompt: Write each number in its group.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Number riddles, harder missing numbers and pattern problems, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Number Detective
resources.subtitle: Use what you know about factors, order and patterns.

sections.title: Number riddles
sections.intro: A prime number has exactly 2 factors. A square number is a number times itself, like 7 x 7 = 49.

example.prompt: I am a square number between 20 and 30. What am I?

items.prompt: I am a square number between 50 and 70. What am I?
I am a prime number between 30 and 40. My digits add to 4. What am I?
List every prime number between 40 and 50.
Which number has the most factors?
items.explain: 18 has 6 factors (1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18). 16 has 5. 19 is prime, so it has 2.

sections.title: Missing number challenges
sections.intro: Times and divide come before plus and take away. Then both sides of the equals sign must be worth the same.

items.prompt: Use 2, 3 and 4 once each, with + and x, to write a number sentence that equals 14. Then find one that equals 10.

sections.title: Pattern problems
sections.intro: A rule that uses the term number lets you jump straight to any term, like term 20.

example.prompt: Term 1 is 7, term 2 is 12, term 3 is 17. What is term 20?
steps: The jump is 5, so start with term x 5.

items.prompt: 1 table seats 6 people, 2 tables in a row seat 8, 3 tables seat 10. How many people can 15 tables seat?
Using the same tables, how many tables are needed for 50 people?
Mia starts with $12 and saves $5 every week. After how many weeks will she first have more than $60?
items.answer: 10 weeks: 12 + 10 x 5 = $62. After 9 weeks she has only $57.

Order from smallest to largest: 1.2, 0.12, 1.02
items.hint: Look at the ones first. Two of them start with 1.

example.prompt: 2 x 6 and 3 x 4 make the same number. What is it?

items.prompt: 3 x 6 and 2 x 9 make the same number. What is it?
Circle the multiple of 4.
Solve 214 x 3.
items.hint: Start with 4 x 3 in the ones.

items.prompt: A boat holds 5 people. 23 people want a ride. How many boats?
items.hint: 23 divided by 5 is 4, with 3 left over. The 3 need a boat too.

items.prompt: 2, 5, 8, 11. Finish the rule: start at 2 and add ___ each time. What comes next?

slides.notes: Session 6 this week: test revision part 1 of 2, number and algebra, ready for tomorrow's maths test.

slides.title: Test revision: how these two sessions work
lines: Two revision sessions before tomorrow's General Maths tests (Grade 5 and Grade 6).
Session 6, 30 minutes: number and algebra, 14 question types.
Session 7, 60 minutes: fractions, measurement, space, data and chance, 40 question types.
Every question slide is a twin of a test question: same format and skill, new numbers.
Short on time? Slides marked OPTIONAL in their notes can be skipped.
Anchor for both sessions: Read it. Work it. Check it.
slides.notes: For you, not the class: twins keep the test honest while every question type gets rehearsed. Skip this slide when teaching.
Before you start: boards and markers for everyone, scrap paper, and print the Revision Worksheet for all, plus a few Extension and Supported copies.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to show what we know about number and algebra, ready for the test.
successCriteria: I can order decimals and find factors and multiples.
I can choose the right operation for a word problem and check it makes sense.
I can find a missing number or a pattern rule and explain how I know.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Tomorrow's test covers the whole year,
so today we'll practise every kind of number question on it.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
SAY: Every question today is a practice twin of a test question,
with different numbers, so you'll know exactly what to do.
notes.prep: SC1 number facts are reachable for all; SC2 word problems is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 missing numbers and rules is the stretch.

slides.title: Read it. Work it. Check it.

visual.banner: Tomorrow's test: show what you know

notes.answer: open - each student names one topic
beats: POINT to the three steps.
SAY: For every question today and tomorrow, we'll do three things.
Read it, work it, check it.
POINT to the Today strip.
SAY: These are the number topics on the test.
Some will feel easy and some won't, and that's fine.
ASK: Which topic do you feel least sure about? Write just that word.
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: one topic word
SCAN boards and tally the topics.
80%+ -> topics spread out: keep the pace, skip the two OPTIONAL slides.
Less -> most chose one topic: slow down on that slide, re-ask at its end.
notes.prep: Finds the weak spots and sets the anchor. 60 to 90 seconds. Optional if short of time: factor pairs, and the add-6 rule.

beats: SAY: Let's start with decimals.
Read it: smallest first. Then compare the ones, then the tenths.
ASK: Can you write these five decimals in order, smallest to largest?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards for where 0.205 and 0.25 sit.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> stack them with the points lined up, fill gaps with zeros, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 0.250 is bigger than 0.205, even though 0.205 looks longer.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: putting 0.205 after 0.25 because it has more digits.
Fix: add a zero to make 0.250, and they compare again.
notes.stretch: Write a decimal that fits between 0.205 and 0.25.
notes.help: Write each decimal in a place value chart, points lined up.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q1: same skill and format, new numbers. Allow about 75 seconds per question slide.

beats: SAY: Every pair here multiplies to make the same number.
ASK: What number do all these factor pairs make?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 30
SCAN boards for 30.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> draw a 5 by 6 array of dots, count them together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 30. Check it with another pair: 3 times 10 is 30 too.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 13 or 11, the sum of one pair.
Fix: say the pair as a times fact, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Is any factor pair of 30 missing? Prove you have them all.
notes.help: Pick one pair and draw it as rows of dots.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows factors are secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q2.

beats: SAY: Here's a quick test for 4.
Look at the last two digits. If they divide by 4, the whole number does.
ASK: Which three numbers are multiples of 4?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards for 118 or 914.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> test 18, 14 and 32 by counting in fours on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 72, 40 and 32 all divide by 4, but 18 and 14 don't.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing every even number.
Fix: even only means it divides by 2, so they test the last two digits.
notes.stretch: Why does checking only the last two digits work?
notes.help: A list of the multiples of 4 up to 100 to check against.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q3: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Use each word once: prime, square, composite

beats: SAY: A prime has exactly two factors.
A square is a number times itself. Composite has more than two factors.
ASK: Can you match each number to one word, using each word once?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 16 square, 15 composite, 13 prime
SCAN boards for 16 and 15.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one board: Why isn't 16 the composite one?
Less -> list the factors of each number on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 16 is 4 times 4, so it's the square. Tick it or fix it.
trap: calling 15 prime because it is odd.
Fix: 3 times 5 is 15, so it has more factors. They rewrite it.
notes.help: Make each number as an array with counters.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q3: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Find A, B, C and D

beats: SAY: In a factor tree, each pair multiplies to make the number above it.
ASK: What are A, B, C and D?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: A 10, B 5, C 2, D 2
SCAN boards for A first.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> ask what times 8 makes 80, write the fact beside the branch, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 times 8 is 80, and 5 times 2 is 10.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: finding A by taking away: 80 take away 8 is 72.
Fix: say the branch as a times fact, and they redo A.
notes.stretch: Keep splitting until every bottom number is prime.
notes.help: Write what times 8 is 80 beside each branch first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q12: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Now some calculating.
Start with the ones, and carry into the next column.
ASK: What is 467 times 6?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2802
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> split it: 400 x 6, 60 x 6, 7 x 6, then add. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 2802. Check it: 500 times 6 is 3000,
so a bit under 3000 makes sense. Tick it or fix it.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit.
Fix: circle each carry, and they redo that column.
notes.stretch: Explain why 2802 is a bit less than 3000 without working it out again.
notes.help: Partition 467 into 400, 60 and 7 and multiply each part.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q7: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which is the best estimate?
slides.prompt: Sam's bills: phone $468, internet $389. Best estimate of the total?

options.misconception: thinks rounding gives the exact answer
does not notice both bills were rounded up

notes.answer: B - a little less than 900 dollars (exact total 857)
beats: SAY: An estimate gets you close. Then decide: a bit more, or a bit less?
ASK: Which is the best estimate for the total of both bills? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for C.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: How do you know it's less?
Less -> round both on the board: 500 and 400, both rounded up. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Both bills were rounded up to make 900,
so the real total is a little less. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing exactly 900.
Fix: ask if 468 is exactly 500, and they choose again.
notes.stretch: Find the exact total. Was your estimate right?
notes.help: Round each bill on a number line.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q9: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: How much does the coach earn?

visual.text: A swim coach teaches 8 kids a day for 5 days. Each kid pays $20 a day.

beats: SAY: Read it first.
There are three numbers here, and we need all of them.
ASK: How much money does the coach earn in total?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 800 dollars
SCAN boards for 160 or 100.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> work it in two steps on the board: kids first, then dollars. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 8 times 5 is 40 kid visits, and 40 times 20 is 800 dollars.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: multiplying only two of the numbers.
Fix: underline all three numbers, and they use each one.
notes.stretch: What if each kid paid 25 dollars? Find the new total.
notes.help: A table: Day 1 to Day 5, kids each day, dollars each day.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q10: same skill and format, new numbers.

visual.text: 203 rowers are going out on the lake. Each boat holds 8 rowers.

beats: SAY: Read it: every rower needs a seat.
That's going to matter for the remainder.
ASK: How many boats are needed so every rower gets a seat?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 26
SCAN boards for 25.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one 26: What happened to the leftover rowers?
Less -> draw 25 boats of 8 and 3 rowers left on the shore, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 203 divided by 8 is 25 remainder 3.
Those 3 rowers still need a boat, so it's 26. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 25, or 25 remainder 3.
Fix: ask where the last 3 rowers sit, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: How many more rowers could fit in the last boat?
notes.help: Count up in eights: 80, 160, 200, then the 3 left over.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q8: same skill and format, new numbers.

visual.text: Ava had $184.60 in her account. She spent $35.25 and $42.10.

beats: SAY: Two things were bought, so we take away both of them.
ASK: How much money is left in Ava's account?
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 107.25
SCAN boards for the decimal points lined up.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> add the two buys first, 77.35, then take it away in columns. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: She spent 77 dollars 35 altogether,
and 184.60 take away 77.35 leaves 107.25. Tick it or fix it.
trap: taking away only one of the purchases.
Fix: tick each amount as it is used, and they finish the subtraction.
notes.stretch: Can Ava buy a 9 dollar snack and keep 100 dollars?
notes.help: Line up the decimal points in a place value grid first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q7: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Times before plus, then balance
steps: Work out the side you can.

beats: MODEL the left side first.
SAY: Watch how I start with the side I can work out.
POINT to 2 x 8.
SAY: There's a times and a plus, so times comes first.
2 times 8 is 16, then 4 plus 16 is 20.
POINT to the equals sign.
SAY: Equals means both sides are worth the same.
So 5 times something must make 20.
ASK: So what is the missing number?
10 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
EXPECT: 4
REVEAL after the choral answer.
SAY: It's 4, because 5 times 4 is 20.
trap: working left to right: 4 plus 2 is 6, times 8 is 48.
Fix: circle the times first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Change one number so the answer is 6.
notes.help: Cover the right side and work out the left first.
notes.prep: The one idea behind two test questions (Grade 5 Q11, Grade 6 Q10): times before plus, then balance both sides. SC3.

slides.title: What is 6 + 3 × 5?
slides.prompt: Write the letter of the answer.

options.misconception: works left to right: 6 + 3 = 9, then times 5

beats: SAY: This one is just for you, so no talking.
ASK: What is 6 plus 3 times 5? Write the letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: Why not 45?
Less -> build 3 groups of 5 counters plus 6 more, count them all, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 21. Times first: 3 times 5 is 15, and 6 more is 21.
Anyone on A starts Your turn on the Supported Worksheet.
trap: writing A, 45.
Fix: circle 3 x 5 first, and they work it out again.
notes.prep: Hinge: under 80% means the counters model before the next two slides.

beats: SAY: Same idea as before: work out the side you can first.
ASK: What is the missing number?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 6
SCAN boards for 24.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> write 24 under the right side, ask: 4 times what is 24? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 72 divided by 3 is 24, and 4 times 6 is 24.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 24, the value of the right side.
Fix: ask what makes 4 times it equal 24, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write your own like this one with a missing number of 9.
notes.help: Cover the left side and work out 72 divided by 3 first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q11: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: More steps now: left side first, then balance.
ASK: What is the missing number?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
SCAN boards for 49 in the working.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one board: How did you check it?
Less -> write 37 on both sides, take off the 2s:
5 times what is 35? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The left side is 2 plus 35, which is 37.
And 5 times 7 plus 2 is 37 too. Tick it or fix it.
trap: working left to right: 2 plus 5 is 7, times 7 is 49.
Fix: circle 5 x 7 first, and they redo the left side.
notes.stretch: Make one like this with an answer of 9.
notes.help: Work out the left side on paper, then try numbers in the box.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q10: same skill and format, new numbers.

answers: Start at 5 and add 6 each time

notes.answer: start at 5 and add 6 each time
beats: SAY: Now patterns. Look at the jump from one number to the next.
ASK: Can you finish this rule: start at 5 and do what each time?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: add 6
SCAN boards for add 6.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> draw the jumps between each pair on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Each number is 6 more than the one before.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing add 5, the first number.
Fix: find the gap between two numbers, and they rewrite the rule.
notes.stretch: What would the 10th number be? How do you know?
notes.help: Write the difference under each jump.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows patterns are secure. Twin of Grade 6 Q12.

slides.title: Find the rule and the 5th term

notes.answer: multiply the term by 4 and add 2. The 5th term is 22
beats: SAY: A rule must work for every term.
ASK: What rule uses the term number, and what is the 5th term?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: times 4, add 2. 22
SCAN boards for add 4.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Test your rule on term 3.
Less -> the jump is 4, so times 4. Compare 4 with 6, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 times 4 plus 2 is 6, and 5 times 4 plus 2 is 22.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: a rule that only fits term 1, like times 6.
Fix: they test it on term 2 and change it.
notes.help: Add a times 4 row under the table and compare.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q11: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Do the revision sheet: the trickiest question types again. Read it, work it, check it.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
CIRCULATE. Start with the students who chose missing numbers on the launch.
TIME: 6 minutes. Do Q3, Q4, Q6 and Q7 first. The rest goes home.
trap: skipping the reading and calculating the first numbers they see.
Fix: they underline what the question asks, then redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: number riddles, harder missing numbers and pattern problems, with worked examples.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: smaller numbers, the first step done and a hint on every question.
notes.prep: Independent practice of every number and algebra question type, with new numbers. The sheet is evidence for SC1 to SC3.
notes.tag: [You Do | Mastery and application | SC2 | HITS 3, 8]

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: 290 students are going on an excursion. Each bus holds 45 students. How many buses are needed?

beats: SAY: Last one, and it's just for you.
Read it, work it, check it.
ASK: How many buses are needed so every student gets a seat?
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
RECORD who writes 6, or 6 remainder 20.
They get two minutes with you during Session 7's Your turn.
trap: writing 6.
Fix: none now. Record the name for Session 7's Your turn.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: choose the operation, then decide what the remainder means.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner which question type you'll check twice tomorrow.

notes.answer: open - listen for a named question type and why
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
ASK: How ready do you feel for the number questions tomorrow?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
A thumb up with 6 buses on the board matters most.
ASK: Tell your partner which question type you'll check twice tomorrow.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: a named question type, like remainders
notes.prep: Read the thumbs beside the exit evidence. The remainder group gets two minutes during Session 7's Your turn.
